-    Caution: marked drowsiness (↑ w EToH/sedatives/tranquilizers) · ask doctor first: breathing problems, glaucoma, trouble urinating (enlrg prostate) · ⍉ use to make a child sleepy · excitability (children)
-    MOA: phenothiazine H1 antagonist (+ D2 block -> antiemetic) -> sedation + anticholinergic
-    Caution: ↓ sz threshold · CI comatose states, phenothiazine hypersensitivity/idiosyncratic rxn
-    BBW: potentially fatal resp depression · CI <2 y (peds ≥2 y: use w caution)

roles.drugs: Glucocorticoids: optional burst then taper; earlier is better (within 24 h beat 25–72 h in one small series); helps vestibular recovery on caloric testing, symptom benefit uncertain (Cochrane 2011: none shown; 2022 meta-analysis: some benefit in the acute phase); your table says first line
